h1: G Hua Hin Resort & Mall — a city resort with its own mall, walkable to Market Village
intro: The "& Mall" in the name is not a gimmick · G Hua Hin Resort & Mall is a city resort with a supermarket, pharmacy and small shops built into the ground floor — take the lift down and you can shop right there · It sits in central Hua Hin on Soi Phetchkasem 94, about a 4-minute walk from Market Village mall, with the beach a short walk across the road · A 4-star resort with 79 rooms, many with wide daybed balconies overlooking the saltwater pool · There is a free shuttle from Hua Hin train station · From approx. ฿1,600/night · scored 9.4 from 126 reviews.

body.html: G Hua Hin Resort & Mall sits in the middle of Hua Hin town on Soi Phetchkasem 94, next to Bangkok Hospital Hua Hin · What sets it apart from an ordinary city resort is that it has a small mall built into the building — a G Supermarket, a pharmacy and retail shops on the ground floor · Plenty of guests say it is genuinely handy on a longer Hua Hin trip: when you want water, snacks or toiletries, you just take the lift down and grab them without leaving the property.

There are 79 rooms, from Deluxe up to Family Suites and a Jacuzzi Spa Suite · The point reviewers agree on is that the rooms are spacious with large balconies and daybeds where you can lounge and look down at the pool · Deluxe rooms start around 40–45 sqm, while suites stretch to 80 sqm · Beds are comfortable, the hot-water showers have good pressure, and there are pool-access rooms you can step straight into the pool from · Overall the rooms are clean and well kept by city-resort standards.
"Brilliant location — you can walk to the mall and restaurants, the rooms are big, the balcony has a daybed to chill on, and the breakfast was tasty with a big choice."

The pool is an outdoor saltwater pool with a separate kids' pool, clear water and a tidy deck · There is a pool bar and the in-house Fingers restaurant · Breakfast earns frequent praise — guests say it is fresh and varied, with both Thai and Western options · The small caveats people mention are that some items can be slow to be topped up when it is busy, and the pool closes fairly early (around 7pm), so late-night swimmers should plan around that.

Location is the trump card here · It is about a 4-minute walk to Market Village mall and not far from BluPort, Cicada Market and the Hua Hin night market · Hua Hin beach is just across the road, a few minutes on foot · Crucially for anyone arriving by train — the resort runs a free shuttle from Hua Hin train station, so you can wheel your bags to the station and call them to collect you, which is ideal if you are not driving · If you do drive, there are two free car parks.

To be straight about it, the thing to understand before booking is that this is a city resort, not an absolute-beachfront one · The beach is walkable but you have to cross busy Phetchkasem Road; you don't step out of your room onto the sand like at a seafront resort · The clearest complaint in reviews is inconsistent front-desk service — some guests report a cool reception and being charged for small extras like additional pillows · It doesn't happen to everyone, but it comes up often enough to flag · There is also just one small lift, which can mean a wait at peak times.

In short, G Hua Hin Resort & Mall suits travellers who want a central, walk-everywhere base with supplies on hand at a sensible price · Standard-season rates start around ฿1,600–2,600/night, climbing over long weekends and high season · If you are doing Hua Hin without a car — walking to eat and shop and taking the train home — it fits that style very well · But if you dream of a resort where you open the door to the sea, look at the beachfront options instead.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for a room with a pool-view balcony and daybed — that is the feature guests love most · If you arrive by train, contact the hotel ahead about the station shuttle · And if you are wary of nickel-and-dime charges, ask at check-in exactly what costs extra (extra beds, pillows) so there are no surprises at checkout.

honestSummary: G Hua Hin Resort & Mall sells convenience — its own shops, walk-everywhere location and a free train-station shuttle at a sensible price · Rooms are big, the daybed balconies are lovely and the saltwater pool is clean · But understand it is not beachfront, and front-desk service can be hit-or-miss.
honestChecks: If you want a beachfront resort where you open the door to the sea — this is in the town centre and you cross Phetchkasem Road to the sand → choose a Khao Takiab or central-beach beachfront resort instead.
If you expect polished, luxury-grade service — reviews note inconsistent front-desk staff and some nickel-and-dime charges → confirm what costs extra at check-in.
If you like late-night swims — the pool closes fairly early, around 7pm → plan your swim for the early evening before it shuts.

faqTitle: FAQ — G Hua Hin Resort & Mall

faq.q: Where is G Hua Hin Resort & Mall · is it on the beach?
faq.a: It sits in central Hua Hin on Soi Phetchkasem 94, next to Bangkok Hospital Hua Hin · It is not directly beachfront, but the beach is a few minutes' walk across Phetchkasem Road · It is about a 4-minute walk to Market Village mall and close to Cicada Market, the night market and the train station.

faq.q: Does it really have a train-station shuttle?
faq.a: Yes · The resort provides a free shuttle from Hua Hin train station, ideal for travellers arriving by rail who are not driving · Contact the hotel ahead to arrange the pick-up time · If you do drive, there are two free car parks.

faq.q: How much does G Hua Hin Resort & Mall cost · what room types are there?
faq.a: Standard-season rates start around ฿1,600/night for a Deluxe Pool View of about 40 sqm · There are Deluxe Pool Access rooms you can step into the pool from, plus Family rooms and Family Suites up to 80 sqm · Rates rise over long weekends and high season, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What is the "& Mall" in the name?
faq.a: It means the hotel has shops built into the building — a supermarket, pharmacy and retail shops on the ground floor · Take the lift down for water, snacks or toiletries without leaving the property · Guests on longer stays say it is very convenient.

faq.q: Who is G Hua Hin Resort & Mall best for?
faq.a: It suits families and travellers who want a central, walk-everywhere base on a sensible budget · There are family rooms, a kids' pool and supplies on hand · It is especially handy for those arriving by train thanks to the station shuttle · It is not for travellers who want an absolute-beachfront resort.

Reviews mention inconsistent front-desk service and some nickel-and-dime charges such as extra pillows or beds — ask at check-in what costs extra · The pool also closes fairly early (around 7pm) and there is only one small lift, which can mean a wait at peak times.
